Accuracy.description:
How precisely the coordinates locate the result, most precise first.

- `rooftop`: the address or POI itself.
- `interpolated`: a house number placed between known neighbours.
- `street`: a point on the street.
- `centroid`: the centre of a mapped area.
- `approximate`: a point standing for something larger, such as a town
  or postcode.

Address.description:
Address parts stated by the source record. Parts the record omits are
absent, not filled in from `context`.

areas.description:
Areas below the locality, outermost first (OSM `addr:suburb`,
`addr:quarter`, `addr:neighbourhood`).

place.description:
Named place the house number belongs to where there is no street
(OSM `addr:place`).

Attribution.description:
A data set an answer comes from and how its licence asks it to be
credited. OpenStreetMap is always first: every answer's areas and labels
come from it.

licence.description:
The licence's name, such as `ODbL 1.0` or `CC BY 4.0`. Absent when
the data set's source states none.

text.description:
Whom to credit, such as `© OpenStreetMap contributors`, or the data
set's name when its licence asks for no credit or is not known.

Brand.description:
A chain: its name and the number of its `brand:wikidata` item. The item
is the chain's, never the place's, so it gives the place no importance.

wikidata.description: Its Wikidata item, such as `Q867662`, a stable id of the chain.

Common.description: Properties shared by forward and reverse results.

address.description: Address parts stated by the source record.

brand.description:
The chain a place belongs to, when its name may not say: "Tankstation
Zanoli" is an Esso. Present only on places.

category.description: POI category, such as `amenity:cafe`. Present only on POIs.

id.description:
Stable ID from the source data, such as `osm:node:123`. Store it to
find the record again: it outlives a Pack rebuild.

label.description: One-line display label: `name` followed by its location.

name.description:
House number and street for an address (`12 King Street West`), or
the name of a street, area or POI.

road_class.description:
The class of road a street is, the most important of its ways, such
as `motorway` or `residential`. Present only on streets.

Context.description:
Areas containing the result, one per tier, most specific first. A tier
the country does not map is absent.

place.description: Named area outside the administrative levels, usually an island.

id.description: Stable ID from the source data, as in a result's `id`.

geocoding.description:
The query, API version and the credits of the data sets the answer
comes from.

query.description:
Query as received, trimmed, with each run of whitespace collapsed to
one space.

confidence.description:
Probability, from 0 to 1, that this is the address the query asks
for. Of results at 0.8, about 8 in 10 are correct. Present only when
the Pack is calibrated. `0` on a `fallback` result.

fallback.description:
`true` when no match was found and the result is the most precise
area the query names instead: its postcode, a town or other area,
its region or its country. `layer` says which. Absent otherwise.

score.description:
Text relevance. Higher is better. Comparable only within one
response: use `confidence` to judge a single result.

ForwardProperties.description: Properties of a forward geocoding result.

ForwardResult.description: One item's result: `response` when it succeeded, `error` when it failed.

error.description: Exactly the Problem `GET` would return for this item.

id.description: The item's `id`, when it sent one.

response.description: Exactly what `GET` returns for this item.

status.description: The status `GET` would have answered this item with.

GeocodeItem.description:
One item of a `/geocode` batch: `GET /geocode`'s parameters and an `id`.

Every field is optional here because the request's query string may give
it for all items. `address` must come from one or the other.

address.description:
The street address on its own: house number and street, without the
town or postcode.

id.description: Echoed in this item's result, to match it up.

limit.description: How many candidates to consider before picking the best.

locality.description: The town or city the address is in.

q.description:
The address as free text. Give `q` or the address fields, not both; a
field sent empty counts as given.

JobEndpoint.description: The lookup every row of a job runs.

JobFormat.description: A job's file format: CSV, or one JSON object a line.

JobState.description: Where a job is: running, or stopped and how.

info.description:
Forward, autocomplete and reverse geocoding of addresses, served from a Pack built from OpenStreetMap and OpenAddresses.

Every response is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Forward results carry a `score`, and a `confidence` when the Pack is calibrated. Reverse results carry a `distance_m`.

Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents (`application/problem+json`). Branch on `error_code`. `title` and `detail` are prose and may change.

get.description:
Geocodes an address to coordinates, given as free text in `q` or as
separate fields. Answers are addresses, streets, postcodes and areas,
never places: those are `/places`'.

With `q`, returns the matches best first, highest `score` first, as many
as `limit`.

With the fields, returns the best match or no result. `address` is
matched on its own, then checked against `locality`, `region` and
`postcode`.

- A house number missing from the data is interpolated between its
  neighbours (`accuracy: interpolated`), or answered with its street
  (`accuracy: street`).
- A street matches `postcode` only when postcode data confirms it.
- A different house is never returned: `10/1367` matches as written or
  as 1367, never as house 10.
- `geocoding.query` is the form of the address that matched, which can
  differ from `address`.

post.description:
The body is a JSON array of items, at most the server's item limit (1000
by default). Each takes the parameters `GET /geocode` takes, plus an
optional `id` echoed in its result. The request's own query-string
parameters apply to every item, and an item's own fields override them:
`?country=CA` scopes every item to Canada.
`QUERY` takes the same body and answers the same: `POST` is for clients
that cannot send `QUERY`.

Each result's `response` is exactly what `GET` returns for its item, and
its `error` the Problem `GET` would return. Results are in input order,
one per item, and a bad item never fails the batch.

post.description:
Geocodes every row of a CSV or JSONL upload. Rows are looked up while the
file uploads, and their results stream back in this response: CSV in the
order rows were sent, JSONL in the order they finish, each line with its
`row`. The results are kept at `Content-Location` for the server's
retention, 72 hours by default.

- CSV: name the columns with `address` (several, comma-separated, are
  joined), `locality`, `region` and `postcode`, or `lat` and `lon` for
  reverse. Without them, the header row's names are matched to common
  ones (`street`, `city`, `zip`, `latitude` and so on). The output is the
  input with `geocode batch`'s `geocode_*` columns added.
- JSONL: each line is a `QUERY /geocode` or `QUERY /reverse` item, and
  `endpoint` is required.

Every other query-string parameter, such as `country`, applies to every
row. Each row's answer is the one its `GET` returns. Send
`Prefer: respond-async` to be answered with the job's status once the
upload is in, instead of with the results.

`QUERY` takes the same body and answers the same: `POST` is for clients
that cannot send `QUERY`.

Each result's `response` is exactly what `GET` returns for its item, and
its `error` the Problem `GET` would return. Results are in input order,
one per item, and a bad item never fails the batch. An item's `ids` is
held to the same limit as `GET`'s, the server's item limit, on its own.
